model_annotation: This horizontal stacked bar chart illustrates the public expenditure as a percentage of GDP (% des BIP) for various European countries in 2021 (light green bars) and the projected increase between 2021 and 2024 (dark blue bars), with each country’s total expenditure represented by the combined length of the two segments. The countries are listed vertically on the y-axis in descending order of total projected expenditure by 2024, starting with Poland at the top and ending with Spain at the bottom. The x-axis represents the percentage of GDP, ranging from 0 to 4%, with major gridlines at 1%, 2%, 3%, and 4%. A vertical black tick mark next to each country indicates a reference value of 1.5% above the 2021 expenditure level. For example, Poland’s 2021 expenditure was approximately 1.8% of GDP, with a projected increase to about 4.1% by 2024, significantly exceeding the reference threshold. In contrast, Spain’s 2021 expenditure was around 0.5% of GDP, rising to approximately 1.3% by 2024, remaining well below the reference level. The chart visually highlights which countries are projected to experience the largest growth in public spending relative to their 2021 levels and how these levels compare to the 1.5%-over-2021 benchmark.
